description: Just Kids with Big Dream—turned into a team! We are HexaByte, building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Valencia City. We welcome passionate developers, designers, and creatives to join us. Let's build something amazing together!
summary: For this challenge, we developed SPUDNAUT: The Great Starch Migration, a 2D lunar habitat training game built with TypeScript, Phaser 3, and live NASA space-weather data for kids ages 7-12. In the year 3042, Earth is buried under potatoes, so ten elite tubers launch under Commander Russet to test whether potato astronauts can keep a Moon station alive. Instead of turning space science into dry engineering datasheets or consequence-free button clicking, SPUDNAUT transforms real lunar survival constraints into playful tension: players balance four interconnected station systems - Life, Power, Research, and Farm - across hands-on room mini-games and respond to real NASA DONKI solar emergencies. Teaching young learners how off-world habitats survive matters as humanity prepares for sustained lunar exploration under Artemis, turning NASA's open space-weather data and life-support science into everyday curiosity, systems thinking, and crisis problem-solving.
details:
How It Works

SPUDNAUT drops kids into a complete Earth-to-Moon habitat simulation built around clear visual tradeoffs and safe experimentation:

• Loadout, Moon Briefing & Launch: Players select one of 4 specialist roles - Repairman (Power), Farmer (Farm), Researcher (Research), or Traveller (Life) - customize one of 12 suit colors, and pick a difficulty tier (Level 1: 15%, Level 2: 30%, or Level 3: 50% storm chance). Visual Moon Hazard Cards introduce 0.166 g lunar gravity, near-vacuum airlessness, and static-charged lunar regolith dust before launching to the base.

• Commander Russet Spotlight Tutorial: On a player's first run, the screen dims to spotlight each HUD element one at a time - upper-left Shift Progress & Tasks, upper-right Map & Settings, and lower-middle 4 Status Bars - alongside first-time mini-game hints that stay out of the way on future runs.

• Pick-3 of 6 Room Missions: Each shift offers 6 candidate tasks drawn from 8 station jobs across dedicated rooms (Hydroponics Bay for Farm, Med Lab for Life, Reactor Dome for Power, and Comms Dome for Research). Players can only choose 3 tasks per shift, weighing visible green +Benefit and red -Disadvantage previews before playing fast, 10-20 second tactile mini-games.

• Live NASA DONKI Disasters & 3-Card Tool Triage: SPUDNAUT queries a rolling 7-days or 14-days NASA DONKI feed (FLR Solar Flares, CME Coronal Mass Ejections, SEP Solar Energetic Particles, and GST Geomagnetic Storms), sorted newest-first. When a warning flags a damaged subsystem, players pick 1 of 3 Tool Cards: the matching tool repairs the hit part, while the wrong tool causes a comedic mishap and automatically rewinds to the last saved checkpoint.

• Shift Celebration & Return Home: Finishing daily tasks earns praise from Commander Russet, and completing the shortened multi-shift tour triggers an Earth-return reward animation before starting fresh runs.

Benefits & Intended Impact

• For Kids (Ages 7-12): Builds practical intuition for resource tradeoffs, interconnected life-support systems, and space-weather cause-and-effect without intimidating jargon or harsh start-over punishments.

• For Classrooms & Educators: Runs directly in modern web browsers (with PWA support, offline fallbacks, and edge-cached DONKI proxy templates) so schools and kiosks avoid DEMO_KEY rate limits.

• Intended Impact: Making NASA telemetry (DONKI) and lunar habitation engineering (ECLSS, static regolith, ~708-hour lunar day/night cycles) genuinely playable so elementary and middle-grade students experience why astronauts make tough engineering compromises.

Tools & Technologies Used

• Game Engine & Frontend: TypeScript, Phaser 3 (HTML5 Canvas / WebGL 2D engine), Vite, custom HTML/CSS HUD overlays, PWA manifest (manifest.webmanifest), and localStorage save/checkpoint persistence.

• Maps, UI & Visual Assets: Tiled map editor (spudnaut-station.tmj room map, collision masks, BFS pathfinding), Figma (layered SVG/PNG cockpit UI), custom SPUDNAUT potato & habitat art, Kenney & Wenrexa sci-fi UI/icon packs (staged via Node scripts), and FFmpeg (audio/splash prep).

• Live Data & Edge Caching: NASA DONKI API (FLR, CME, SEP, GST) paired with Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge Functions (900s cached proxy templates) plus curated offline Space Apps fallback cards.

• Testing & QA: Vitest unit/simulation tests and a custom Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) end-to-end verification runner.

Creative Approach & Team Design Considerations

• Satire Grounded in Real Physics: Wrapping lunar systems engineering inside a comedic 3042 potato migration keeps 7-12-year-olds hooked while every crisis obeys real Moon constraints and live NASA solar alerts.

• Controlled Cognitive Load: Narrowing station management to 4 always-visible bars (Life, Power, Research, Farm), shortened runs, pick-3-of-6 choices, and automatic checkpoint retries prevents kid fatigue while preserving real tradeoff tension.

• Scientific Transparency & Scope: Official Moon data and live DONKI events drive the world rules, while 0-100 bars and task numbers remain simplified educational game values - never claiming flight-certified operational accuracy. The current release scopes exclusively to the Moon station scenario.
